\*Data above 298 K estimated. Phase changes: 828 K, $\alpha-\beta$ transition point of Sr; $\Delta H^{\circ}=0.180$ kcal/mol. 1041 K, melting point of Sr; $\Delta H^{\circ} = 1.960$ kcal/mol. 1654.1 K, boiling point of Sr; $\Delta H^{\circ} = 32.730$ kcal/mol. Heat capacity (cal/mol·K) and enthalpy (kcal/mol) equations: 298.15-2000 K: $Cp^{0} = 12.021 + 1.416 \times 10^{-3} T - 0.714 \times 10^{5} T^{-2}$ $H^{0} - H_{298}^{0} = 12.021 \times 10^{-3} T + 0.708 \times 10^{-6} T^{2} + 0.714 \times 10^{2} T^{-1} - 3.886$ Reaction equations (kcal/mol):
298.15-828 K: $\Delta Hr^{\circ} = -128.360 + 3.255 \times 10^{-3} \text{T} - 1.984 \times 10^{-6} \text{T}^{2} + 62.950 \text{T}^{-1}$
$\Delta Gr^{\circ} = -128.360 - 3.255 \times 10^{-3} \text{T} \ln T + 1.984 \times 10^{-6} \text{T}^{2} + 31.475 \text{T}^{-1} + 44.378 \times 10^{-3} \text{T}$
828-1041 K: $\Delta Hr^{\circ} = -126.597 - 1.151 \times 10^{-3} \text{T} + 0.548 \times 10^{-6} \text{T}^{2} + 37.250 \text{T}^{-1}$
$\Delta Gr^{\circ} = -126.597 + 1.151 \times 10^{-3} \text{T} \ln T - 0.548 \times 10^{-6} \text{T}^{2} + 18.625 \text{T}^{-1} + 14.760 \times 10^{-3} \text{T}$
1041-1654.1 K: $\Delta Hr^{\circ} = -129.182 - 0.551 \times 10^{-3} \text{T} + 0.548 \times 10^{-6} \text{T}^{2} + 37.250 \text{T}^{-1}$
$\Delta Gr^{\circ} = -129.182 + 0.551 \times 10^{-3} \text{T} \ln T - 0.548 \times 10^{-6} \text{T}^{2} + 18.625 \text{T}^{-1} + 21.411 \times 10^{-3} \text{T}$
1654.1-2000 K: $\Delta Hr^{\circ} = -158.059 - 2.424 \times 10^{-3} \text{T} + 1.523 \times 10^{-6} \text{T}^{2} - 5623.450 \text{T}^{-1}$
$\Delta Gr^{\circ} = -158.059 + 2.424 \times 10^{-3} \text{T} \ln T - 1.523 \times 10^{-6} \text{T}^{2} - 2811.725 \text{T}^{-1} + 27.636 \times 10^{-3} \text{T}$
Source: Data from Chase (17) who estimated all above 298 K.
